  {FABL.fourierCoeff_majority_two_mul_add_one}
  {direct}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b003,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b004,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p123-b001}
\difficulty{3}
Let $m,j$ be nonnegative integers, and let $S$ be a subset of the coordinates in the
sign cube of dimension $2m+1$ with $|S|=2j+1$. The absolute Fourier coefficient of
majority on $S$ equals $\frac{\binom{m}{j}}{\binom{2m}{2j}}$ times the odd-majority
influence in dimension parameter $m$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{6}
Let $m,j$ be nonnegative integers with $j<m$. On the sign cube of dimension $2m+1$, take
subsets $S,T$ with $|S|=2j+1$ and $|T|=2(j+1)+1$. The absolute Fourier coefficient of
majority on $T$ equals $(2j+1)/(2m-2j-1)$ times the absolute Fourier coefficient on $S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Strict decrease of majority coefficients]
\lean{FABL.abs_fourierCoeff_majority_next_odd_lt}

\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.abs_fourierCoeff_majority_next_odd_eq, FABL.abs_fourierCoeff_majority_two_mul_add_one, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.majority, FABL.oddMajorityInfluence_pos}
\difficulty{4}
Let $m,j$ be nonnegative integers such that $2j+3\le m$. On the sign cube of dimension
$2m+1$, take subsets $S,T$ with $|S|=2j+1$ and $|T|=2(j+1)+1$. The absolute Fourier
coefficient of majority on $T$ is strictly smaller than the absolute Fourier coefficient
on $S$.
\end{theorem}
